memos.risk:
Risk officer assessment: I recommend refusing any size.

Key red flags in the brief:
- Drawdown of 59% from the 30-minute high, with a -35% return in the last 15 minutes and net outflow. Momentum is broken.
- Sell-to-buy ratio of 0.96 in the first two minutes after graduation, plus a launch bot present, and 1,473 sellers in the last 15 minutes against 1,587 buyers.
- Curve bundle share of 57% and completer share of 49% suggest coordinated activity, not organic demand.
- Pool depth of 130 SOL is thin for a $20 ticket. Round-trip costs of 1.4-5.1% would be at the high end here.

The "ORGANIC" label doesn't override the flow data. Nearly all of the trading volume ($240k) is churn, and the coin is already well off its high.

Sizing if the desk overrides: $5 minimum, 50% stop, 15-minute hold. But I would not approve this. The base rate for buying a coin in this state is poor, and a skipped coin costs nothing.
memos.scout:
The case for buying is weak. The strongest point is organic-looking distribution: top-3 share is 6.1%, buyers are 943, and the class is ORGANIC with no airdrop dump. Pool depth of 130 SOL keeps slippage manageable for a $20 ticket.

But the brief's recent action argues hard against entry. The coin is down 35% over the last 15 minutes and 59% off its 30-minute high, with net flow negative (-9.89 SOL) and a sell-to-buy ratio near 1.0 right after graduation. Sellers (1,473) nearly match buyers (1,587) in the last window, so demand is not holding. The 30-minute return of +122% is already retraced, meaning the early buyers are exiting into the dip.

Half the curve buys came from bundles (56.5%), and the launch bot was present, which weakens the "organic" label. Demand that is fading, plus a bundled curve, does not meet the bar of real demand still present in 30-60 minutes.

Verdict: no honest case to buy now. Skip.
memos.skeptic:
The most likely loss path is a distribution from the post-graduation holders, the same mechanism that makes "organic" coins bleed. The last 15 minutes show net flow of -9.89 SOL, a sell-to-buy ratio near 1 and 1,473 sellers against 1,587 buyers, with price down 35% and 59% off the 30-minute high. Early buyers are exiting, not accumulating.

Bundling is also heavy: bundle_share is 0.57 and completer_share 0.49, so much of the curve was assembled by coordinated wallets that can exit together. The launch bot in the first two minutes and a 0.96 sell-to-buy ratio point the same way.

With a 130 SOL pool, a $20 round trip at 1.4-5.1% fees still leaves room for a dead-volume drift down. Skip.
